chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Ali al-Ahmasi, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him), from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
By Allah, he will not be saved from the sin except the one who acknowledges it.
He said, and Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) said: Regret suffices as repentance.
ai.seo_question: What is the role of regret in Islamic repentance?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (AS) links the external act of confession with the internal state of remorse, establishing that sincere regret (nadam) is the essence of repentance. This hadith underscores the Shia scholarly view that true tawbah requires both recognition of the sin and a heartfelt turning back to God, ensuring that the believer does not remain in spiritual stagnation.
